problem_class_challenge.finding: The prior round judged this anchored_to_scale and prescribed restating the class as where the drive LIVES so that it cannot be skipped or claimed, rather than which moment a gate schedules it at. The title and the framing are unchanged at version 3, so the same verdict stands, and it is now worse than a leftover: the record chose an option whose own summary opens "No record and no scheduling question", under a title that asks "and at what moment". A record whose title states a question its decision dissolves cannot be read by anybody later without re-deriving what was actually decided. Two measurements of this reviewer's own, both against the premise the title carries, that a drive is an operation on the working tree. ONE, the premise is not forced: the chosen mechanism, built and driven here for VELDO-0001 AC1, applies the declared mutation to an in-process module copy at 0.0024 s per drive, mean of 20, so the whole population of 227 behaviour-bearing criteria costs 0.55 s of copying, and the tree is never touched. TWO, the cost figures that generated the ordering of the four original options reproduce exactly and refute the ordering rather than supporting it: the unit stage is 106.8 s here against the 105.8 s the record cites, the twelve VELDO-era fragments cost 11.7 s together, the per-criterion sum over the 61 criteria of VELDO-0001 to VELDO-0012 is 59.79 s, the sum over all 146 mechanically attributable criteria at per-suite granularity is 1777 s or 29.6 min, and the 4.3 h that the every-run dead end rests on is 146 times the full stage. Stated as a class the problem is that a declared property's FALSIFIABILITY is never exercised, and PLAN-0018 C2 already states the class-level answer the record still does not adopt as its own title: the proof IS a driven mutation with the mutation asserted to have applied.

option_challenges.finding: This reviewer independently reproduces the prior round's refutation and agrees with it, so only the new part is spelled out. Reproduced on a throwaway copy: unit stage 106.8 s; fragment 17 closure 0.065 s; the twelve VELDO-era fragments 11.7 s together; the per-criterion sum for the 61 criteria of the twelve motivating items 59.79 s; all 146 attributable criteria 1777 s at per-suite granularity against 4.33 h under the full-suite reading the dead end silently assumes. The dead end's own arithmetic ("4530 assertions across 34 suites") reads the suite as indivisible while scripts/suites/requires.json ships a measured per-fragment closure for every one of the 34, so the granularity the dead end is stated at is not the granularity the falsified_by clauses name. THE NEW FINDING IS AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION AT VERSION 3. The chosen option drives every criterion on every run of its own suite. That IS every-run, at a granularity this dead end does not distinguish, so version 3 simultaneously refuses driving on every run as unaffordable and chooses driving on every run as the mechanism. Measured, the chosen granularity is affordable: 227 module copies cost 0.55 s and the criterion rows that would be re-executed are 1031 of the 4134 literal assertion labels, each attributed to exactly one criterion, so the added row work is a quarter of the corpus and not a second corpus. Either this dead end is rewritten to say WHICH every-run is dead (the one where each drive re-runs all 34 suites in a subprocess) or it reads as a refusal of the option that was chosen.

The conclusion holds, and this reviewer confirms the prior round's finding that the REASON the record gives for it is false about this repository's own ledger, because that reason survives unedited into version 3 after a bound review documented it in detail. Ledger finding 40 says both vacuous VELDO-0007 criteria were mutation-to-row relationships inside the item's own files, an accept-either-outcome assertion and a guard living in a function no row called, not out-of-footprint dependencies. Version 3 still asserts that an out-of-footprint dependency "is exactly how the two vacuous VELDO-0007 criteria survived". This matters more at round two than at round one: the framing uses this false reason to eliminate an option, a bound review corrected it with citations, and the correction was not applied while an option was added on the same review's authority. The dead end's real support, unchanged from the prior round and still uncited in the record, is findings 34, 35 and 62, teeth depending on CPython glob behaviour, teeth destroyed by an unrelated sibling row being red, and a fixture that reddened only in the union of nine items. And .veldo/validate_checks.py:258 still records in its own docstring that enforcing the declared footprint against the actual diff is WARP-1102 and is not done, so the footprint remains a structurally validated declaration with nothing comparing it to what a commit touched.

Holds, and understated in exactly the way the prior round measured; version 3's note now agrees, so this reviewer records agreement and adds only what the note still leaves out. The forgery surface was not removed by choosing a different option, it was RELOCATED. Under proof-time-record the artifact the gate reads is a YAML record the author writes; under in-suite-paired-control the artifact is a mutation the author writes in Python, in the same suite fragment as the assertion it is supposed to falsify, and nothing compares that mutation against the criterion's prose falsified_by clause. The record's own eliminating phrase for changed-footprint applies unchanged: it trusts the same declaration it is meant to be checking. The ledger has recorded four times that the author's own test code is precisely where teethless checks get written (findings 42, 48, 56 and 60, two of them written within an hour of each other by the person documenting the class), so moving the falsification INTO that artifact class is not obviously safer than a record, it is less visible, because a reviewer diffs a new YAML file and nobody diffs a test's mutation against a spec's prose. That is a reason to add the mutation-as- data missing option below, not a reason to keep this one.

Holds, for the reason given and for the stronger reason the prior round added, which this reviewer confirms rather than repeats: a sampling floor bounds an average and every measured incident in the ledger is a statement about one specific criterion on the day it landed, findings 34, 40, 45, 46, 53, 56 and 60, with finding 60 being two teethless checks by one author inside one hour, a rate no rotation period bounds. One addition specific to version 3. Under the chosen option this option is not merely dominated on cost, it is INEXPRESSIBLE: rotation needs persistent state saying whose turn it was, and persistent state is the artifact the chosen option exists to delete. So if the chosen option is ever narrowed to a subset for cost reasons, the subset cannot be a rotation without reintroducing the record, and the record must say so or the cheap retreat from a cost problem will quietly rebuild the option this framing rejected twice.

THE DEAD END IS AIMED AT THE WRONG FAILURE, and both clauses it does state are weaker than it thinks. CLAUSE ONE, seam reachability, is honest and is the minority it claims: measured over the 227 behaviour-bearing criteria that declare a falsification, 159 clauses name only .py subjects and 68 name a non-.py subject or no path at all, of which 43 name no path at all and 6 name a shell script or the gate. So the residue is 68 of 227, 30 percent, and the record's "the majority and NOT all" holds, though the record still does not NAME the residue it says must be named rather than assumed empty. CLAUSE TWO is not a dead end at all, it is an absent measurement: "the in-memory cost is UNMEASURED as of version 3". This reviewer measured it by building the mechanism. VELDO-0001 AC1's declared mutation, deleting the per-criterion loop in falsification_problems, applied to the source of .veldo/validate_checks.py with the substitution count asserted non-zero, exec'd as a module copy in memory and wired the way validate.py wires the real one: the refusing fixture goes from 2 problems to 0, the accepting fixture stays accepted, and the whole drive costs 0.0024 s, mean of 20 iterations. All 227 criteria therefore cost 0.55 s of copying, and the rows that would be re-executed are 1031 of the 4134 literal labels. The cost clause does not bite. WHAT THE DEAD END MISSES IS THE ONLY THING THAT DECIDES THE OPTION, and it is structural rather than empirical. A mutation applied to a module COPY is not applied to the object the shipped assertion runs against, and this suite architecture says so about itself in two places. Fragment 17's docstring: the rows are driven through V._VC, "the module instance .veldo/validate.py itself loaded and handed the ONE front-matter parser and the ONE failure reporter, so these assertions exercise the same object the validator uses rather than a second copy with test wiring". shared.py's docstring: "THERE IS ONE NAMESPACE AND IT IS THIS MODULE'S ... a fragment that REBINDS a name here changes what every later fragment sees", and scripts/suites/manifest.json records that suite_equiv over this manifest returns DEFECTIVE with every fragment PASSES_IN_AGGREGATE_FAILS_ALONE and the reversed order ORDER_DEPENDENT. Both horns driven by this reviewer. HORN ONE: after the drive, the mutated copy is not the shipped object and the shipped instance still answers unmutated, so every shipped row stayed green while the falsification "passed". That is a criterion proving its teeth against a path the gate does not run, which is ledger finding 40's defect verbatim, a mutation reaching a different path from the row, and it is reachable here BY DEFAULT rather than by mistake. HORN TWO: rebinding the shared name to reach the real row succeeds and leaks, driven, the later fragments now read the mutated module, and the leak is invisible to every observation the record carries because nothing in the tree changed and assumption revert-is-clean's entire signal is git status plus a digest of the TOUCHED FILES. So the option's claim that "nothing is written down, no party has to be trusted, no tree edit happens and there is nothing to revert" is true about the TREE and false about the thing that now carries the risk: there is a namespace to revert, in a namespace the repository has already measured as order dependent, and the record removed the only isolation property it had while pointing the survivor at the wrong subject. A third gap, smaller and worth one sentence: the mutation is re-derived from the criterion's prose on every run by whoever writes the fragment, and 43 of the 227 clauses name no path at all, so for those the in-suite mutation cannot be derived mechanically from what the criterion says.

missing_options.summary: Make the declared falsification MACHINE-APPLICABLE in the spec, being the subject, the pattern and the replacement as data, so whichever lane drives it applies the criterion's own mutation rather than one re-authored at drive time by the party under test.
missing_options.finding: This is upstream of all five options and none of them contains it, which is why the forgery surface moved rather than closed when the chosen option replaced the record. Every option assumes a prose falsified_by clause can be turned into a mutation by whoever drives it, and that turning is a human act each time. Measured: of the 227 behaviour-bearing criteria that declare a falsification, 43 name no path at all in the clause, so for those there is nothing to apply mechanically and the drive is whatever the driver decided it meant; the 12 drives this repository has actually recorded were each hand-built by a reviewer from prose. Under the chosen option this is sharper than under a record, because the mutation now lives in the author's own suite fragment beside the assertion it must falsify, unchecked against the criterion, and the ledger records four times over that the author's own test code is where teethless checks get written (findings 42, 48, 56, 60). Precedent in tree: scripts/check_first_use.py already carries its mutations as a MUTATIONS table with the stated extension rule "A NEW ENTRY IN MUTATIONS, never a pattern match", and .veldo/validate_checks.py already parses each clause structurally, so this is a field on an existing artifact rather than a new organ. It is also the only thing that makes an in-suite control auditable: with the mutation as data, the control and the criterion can be compared, and without it the control is one more self-authored assertion.

missing_options.summary: Drive the SHIPPED assertion in a child interpreter per criterion, with the module under test shadowed by its mutated source, so the mutation reaches the row the criterion names without any shared namespace to leak into.
missing_options.finding: The framing has never contained the option that survives this review's attack on the chosen one. In-suite driving must either mutate a copy, which leaves the shipped row green and proves nothing about it, or rebind the shared module, which mutates a namespace shared by all 34 fragments that scripts/suites/manifest.json already reports ORDER_DEPENDENT and DEFECTIVE. A child process removes the fork: the parent writes the mutated module into a throwaway directory that precedes the real one on the path, runs the criterion's own suite closure in the child, and requires the criterion's row set to red while the paired control stays green, with the parent's own namespace untouched by construction. The cost is already measured and is the cost this framing was arguing about: 59.79 s for the 61 criteria of the twelve motivating items and 1777 s for all 146 attributable ones, and the isolation is the practice this repository already follows everywhere it drives anything, scripts/check_first_use.py copying the tree twice and stating in its docstring that other lanes edit scripts/suites while it runs. It also composes with the landing union below, which no in-process control can, and it needs no seam per criterion, which the prior review named as the chosen option's largest cost.

missing_options.summary: Re-execute the drive at LANDING over the union of what is landing, in the integration slot that already drives mutations, rather than only inside each item's own suite.
missing_options.finding: The prior review named this and version 3 dropped it with no reason recorded, and it is the one thing the chosen option cannot do by construction, so the drop is a loss of coverage rather than a simplification. Ledger finding 62 is the evidence and it is unanswered at version 3: "each of the nine remediation copies was GREEN on its own and the interaction existed only in the union ... Nine green copies are not a green repository, and the only thing that found this was one gate over all of them at once." An in-suite paired control is per suite, per copy, and green in each copy, which is precisely the state finding 62 says is not evidence. Ledger finding 35 is the same fact one level down and also unaddressed: a criterion's only teeth were destroyed by an unrelated sibling row being red, so teeth are a function of suite STATE, and a control that runs inside that state without asserting the state was green first can pass on a suite where the criterion has no teeth at all. The slot exists: scripts/check_first_use.py already copies the tree, applies a sanctioned mutation, proves it landed, runs the whole suite and compares against a baseline, in the integration slot of the gate, at a documented cost of about one nested selftest.

missing_options.summary: Name the drive in the L2 review contract, so the party that has actually produced every measured yield keeps doing it under a contract rather than by habit.
missing_options.finding: Also named by the prior review, also dropped at version 3, and the record's own context paragraph is still the argument for it: the motivation is that "the twelve independent reviews of PLAN-0018 drove them by hand and the result is the reason this record exists". The chosen option relocates the drive to the party whose criterion is under test and removes it from the party whose driving produced the evidence. docs/method.md locates it in review, .veldo/policy.yaml already requires one L2 review at standard and high and two at critical at min_independence L2, so the dispatch and the independence are already paid for. This is not an alternative to the chosen mechanism and should not be recorded as one: it is the lane that catches the mutation that was written to pass, which is the failure an author-written in-suite control cannot catch about itself. WARP-0730's constraint applies and is easy to honour, in that a review REPORTS and never certifies.

assumption_challenges.finding: Load bearing, because it is still the only quantity that discriminates the options, and now mis-specified in a third way on top of the two the prior round measured. Unchanged and still wrong: the signal measures ONE drive while every policy turns on the per-run TOTAL, and the breach threshold "more than the entire current gate" is a moving denominator that .veldo/tripwire.py cannot express, since a reading must carry either a value with a comparator and a threshold it can parse or a manual review with an expiry. THE NEW DEFECT IS THAT THE SIGNAL NO LONGER DESCRIBES THE CHOSEN MECHANISM. It reads "one complete drive over this repository, being mutate, run the named suite, revert", and the chosen option abolishes all three of those verbs: nothing is mutated on disk, no named suite is run as a separate act, nothing is reverted. A tripwire whose signal names an operation the decision removed will be answered either by a reading of the wrong thing or by nothing at all. Worse, the breach clause concludes "at which point only proof-time recording survives as an option", and the record's own note says proof-time-record did not survive, so a live assumption's breach clause now points at a refuted option as the fallback. Re-measured, the quantity itself is comfortable at every granularity that matters: the module copy the chosen mechanism needs is 0.0024 s, mean of 20, so 227 criteria cost 0.55 s; the unit stage is 106.8 s; the twelve VELDO-era fragments are 11.7 s; 61 criteria at per-suite granularity are 59.79 s; 146 are 1777 s. Restate the signal over the per-run total of the chosen mechanism, with a comparator the tripwire organ parses, and delete the fallback clause.

Load bearing under every option including the chosen one, and now in the worst possible state: the record's own decision note DOCUMENTS the breach while the assumption's statement, signal and breach clause are unedited, so version 3 says in one place that a criterion does not resolve to one assertion and in another that it does. Re-measured over the read-only tree, and this is the one figure in the note that does not reproduce. The population is 227 exactly, and the label corpus is 4134 literal labels plus 133 built dynamically, both matching the prior round exactly. Attribution by adjacency, the spec id immediately followed by the criterion id, gives 10 criteria resolving to exactly one row, 81 to none and 136 to more than one, median 5 and maximum 32, which reproduces REV-DEC-0001 to the digit. A looser containment match, spec id and criterion id anywhere in the label, gives 16, 73 and 138, median 6 and maximum 33. The note's 6, 80 and 141 is produced by neither, while its median 6 and maximum 33 belong to the second method, so the note has combined the bucket statistics of one measurement with bucket counts that no measurement here yields, in the direction that strengthens its own conclusion. The conclusion survives anyway: at 10 or at 16, a one-row lookup is unbuildable for 217 or 211 of 227, so the finding is that a re-measurement was asserted and did not reproduce, not that the choice was wrong. THE LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY IS STILL NOT WHAT THE RECORD SAYS. It is that a criterion's ROW SET is mechanically derivable and non-empty, which holds for 146 of 227 today, that at least one member reds under the declared mutation, and that the paired control does not. Left as written, this assumption fires on day one under a breach clause that declares the whole mechanism ungateable.

Not load bearing, and at version 3 it is worse than the wrong proxy the prior round found it to be: under the chosen option it CANNOT BREACH. Its breach is "any drive leaves a modified or untracked file behind", and the chosen option's own summary is that "no tree edit happens and there is nothing to revert", so the only readings this tripwire can ever take are zero, which .veldo/tripwire.py will accept forever against any comparator. A record whose entire subject is that a declared falsification is worth nothing until it is driven is about to ship a monitored assumption that cannot fail. That is the record reproducing its own defect class inside itself, the pattern ledger finding 48 names as reading a finding not inoculating you against it. And the property it is standing in for has moved, which is the part that must not be lost: the chosen option's real isolation question is the SUITE NAMESPACE, not the tree. Driven here: rebinding the shared module name to reach a shipped row leaks the mutated module to every later fragment, in the one namespace shared.py says all 34 fragments execute into, and git status plus a digest of touched files sees exactly none of it, because no file was touched. Ledger finding 53 already refuted this signal from the other side, that git status is blind to every path outside the repository and every ignored path inside it and that a content-only inventory could not see a mutation writing identical bytes. Replace it with isolation stated over the namespace the drive runs in: the shared bindings and sys.modules identical before and after every drive, asserted per drive, which is both true under the chosen option and capable of being false.

Load bearing, correctly identified, and now insufficient in a way that is SPECIFIC to the option version 3 chose, which is why this is not a repeat of the prior round's note. Its signal, a non-zero substitution count plus a changed digest, is satisfied in full by the drive this reviewer ran against a module COPY, where the substitution landed, the digest changed, the predicate flipped, and every shipped assertion in the suite stayed green because the copy is not the object the rows use. So under the chosen option "the mutation landed" and "the mutation landed where the check lives" come apart, and this assumption only asserts the first. That is ledger finding 34's defect with the sign reversed: there a mutation named a line the item never changes and was a no-op, here a mutation applies perfectly to an object nothing gates on. The complete condition is already written down in the repository and still absent from this record: PLAN-0018 says of the twelve reviews that "the mutation landed, was diffed, and reddened the row its own field names, with the paired control staying green so no refusal is a blanket one", and ledger findings 35 and 46 are the two halves the record omits, a drive from a non-green baseline proving nothing and a mutation that reds the right row for the wrong reason not being evidence. Add that as its own assumption before this is built, and extend this one to require that the mutated module is the object the criterion's rows resolve to, since that is now the failure that is reachable by default rather than by mistake.

problem_class_challenge.finding: The problem class is stated against the lifetime of a growing system (instance count and producer count both rising), not against how few instances run today, so it resists the "it is only one process today" anchor that constraint C6 forbids. The attack could not find a scale assumption hiding inside the framing.

option_challenges.finding: The dead_end holds under attack: detection latency and query load both scale with the instance count, a rare change is paid for on every poll of every instance, and there is no version at which constant polling becomes a real event stream. It stops working exactly where the framing says it does.

The dead_end holds: the notification path is bound to one database engine and its connection ceiling, so a second datastore or a non-database producer cannot emit the same signal without a translation shim, and the listener count is capped by the connections the engine will hold open. The attack confirms this is a real dead_end, not a hypothetical one.

The stated dead_end (an operational dependency to run and monitor, over-built where there is genuinely one producer and one consumer forever) holds as written, and the framing is honest that a cross-instance change-notification path is not that degenerate case. The cost is real but it is the accepted cost of the only option that survives the problem class.

missing_options.summary: A transactional outbox with change-data-capture feeding the bus.
missing_options.finding: The framing did not enumerate an outbox/CDC option that writes change intent in the same transaction as the state change and relays it to the bus. It is arguably a refinement of pubsub_bus rather than a distinct option, so it does not overturn the framing, but a human deciding should know it exists as a delivery-guarantee variant.

assumption_challenges.finding: Load bearing and correctly chosen: if the number of instances that must observe a change did NOT grow, db_poll would be defensible, so this assumption is exactly what rules the cheap option out. The attack agrees it is the real hinge.

Load bearing: the moment a second producer type appears, db_listen_notify needs a shim, so this assumption is what separates the single-engine options from the bus. Its signal (count of distinct producer types) is the right thing to watch.

Load bearing: reconcile-on-reconnect via a version or etag is what makes the bus correct under reconnect gaps; if a consumer assumed exactly-once delivery with no reconcile path, the chosen shape would be unsafe. This is a genuine load-bearing assumption, not a decorative one.

old.recommendation: The framing survives the attack. Each cheap option has a dead_end that holds, the problem class is stated honestly, and the recorded assumptions are the real load-bearing ones. The outbox/CDC variant is worth surfacing as a delivery-guarantee refinement of the bus option. This review informs the human; the choice remains the human's to make on the record.
